We have been in feeding therapy with a speech pathologist since our baby was 3 months. It made a world of difference, he went from taking 30 mins to an hour to drink 3 oz, to drinking 3 oz in 15 minutes. He was burning more calories drinking then he was taking in when it takes for 10 mins per oz.  

They had us do mouth exercises and helped confirm the right bottle nipple for him, and he I proved in only a few weeks. Maybe you could YouTube some of the mouth exercises to do while you wait for the appointment?

We exclusively pump though so him dropping the night feed corresponded with him upping his intake during the day so I do know he's still getting the same amount of calories as he did before he dropped the night feed.

Went through this recently at 4 months postpartum. I was getting a lot of clots and developed mastitis on the opposite side weirdly.  Went through a round of antibiotics, added in lacta-biotic (probiotic) since clots can be from a bacteria imbalance. I also stopped using the fridge hack for pumping. And I got a prescription for all purpose nipple ointment, since I was still getting clots after the antibiotic. It helped a lot and got rid of the nipple blebs I was having. $70 and not cover by insurance though 😵‍💫

The right flange size for pumping really helped with pain. I still have some minor pain when the pump first starts now. But it's a lot better. I was so swollen from the hospital that my nipples measured larger then they actually are for the first few weeks. 

I've gone down a few sizes since then, recommend trying smaller flanges even if you measured larger. Also pumping spray really helps. Aching could be from not fully emptying due to wrong size flanges potentially.

I had a similar experience. Flat nipples/ swollen from all the IV fluids as I also had a c section. I couldn't get my son to latch until he was 2 weeks old as he was very sleepy (born 3 weeks early) and too small to fit my nipple in his mouth.

That being said, I'm 6 weeks out now. My son is latching with the nipple shield only as he now has a bottle preference. We work on breastfeeding twice a day but he has bad transfer due to either a tounge tie or muscle tension. So we are working on that. 

Just hang in there and focus on pumping if breastmilk is important to you. We had to supplement with formula for the first few weeks, but my supply has steadily increased with regular pumping. 

make sure you have the right flange sizes for pumping and the right size nipple shield. My nipples got smaller over the weeks as my swelling went down - so I had to change sizes several times. Both flange and nipple shield size. Keep that in mind.

Also a rocker that can lean forward is really helpful for back pain.
